title: charged ads$_{3}$ black branes as marginally deformed two-dimensional cfts
abstract: we study how boundary correlation functions encode the charge dependence of the renormalised euclidean action of an ads$_3$ black brane. in three-dimensional einstein-maxwell theory, the maxwell field has logarithmic asymptotics and is locally dual to a massless pseudoscalar. in the canonical ensemble, the charge density fixes the slope of a spatially linear source for the dual marginal operator. at fixed temperature, the classical action is even in the charge density due to reflection symmetry $φ\to-φ$, and its charge expansion coefficients are governed by catalan numbers. we compute the quadratic and quartic terms from connected correlation functions around the neutral brane. the scalar two-point function and the shift symmetry of its source determine the matter weyl anomaly, which fixes the logarithmic temperature dependence of the quadratic term in the charge expansion. at quartic order, the connected four-point function comes from tree-level graviton exchange. integrating it against the linear source, with an infrared cutoff on the overall scale of the integral, reproduces the quartic coefficient of the action per unit length. at each higher order, the corresponding catalan coefficient predicts the integrated sum of all connected tree-level witten diagrams.

title: existence and multiplicity of $l^2$-normalized solutions for the periodic schrödinger system of hamiltonian type
abstract: in this paper, we study the following nonlinear schrödinger system of hamiltonian type \begin{equation*} \left\{\begin{array}{l} -δu+v(x)u=\partial_v h(x,u,v)+ωv,\ x \in \mathbb{r}^n, \\ -δv+v(x)v=\partial_u h(x,u,v)+ωu,\ x \in \mathbb{r}^n, \\ \displaystyle\int_{\r^n}|z|^2dx=a^2, \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} where the potential function $v(x)$ is periodic, $z:=(u,v):\r^n\rightarrow \r\times\r$, $ω\in \r$ appears as a lagrange multiplier, $a>0$ is a prescribed constant. the existence and multiplicity of $l^2$-normalized solutions for the above schrödinger system are obtained. the proof combines a constrained variational reduction, compactness estimates, and a ljusternik--schnirelmann type multiplicity theorem. in addition, a bifurcation result is also given.

title: a blow-up approach for a priori bounds in semilinear planar elliptic systems: the brezis-merle critical case
abstract: we establish uniform a priori estimates for solutions of semilinear planar hamiltonian elliptic systems in a ball with dirichlet boundary conditions. we consider a broad class of coupled nonlinearities with asymptotic critical behaviour in the sense of brezis--merle. the approach we follow is based on a blow-up analysis combined with liouville--type theorems and integral estimates. our results extend the scalar theory of uniform a priori bounds to the hamiltonian case, and solve an open problem in [de figueiredo d.g., do ó j.m., ruf b., adv. nonlinear stud. 6 (2006), no. 2]. we believe that this approach is new in this setting. as a consequence of our a priori estimates, we prove the existence of a positive solution by means of fixed-point index theory.

title: on blow-up dynamics for the nonlinear wave equation and the harmonic map heat flow
abstract: this ph.d. thesis concerns the blow-up analysis, and more precisely, the asymptotic decomposition into profiles of solutions to nonlinear partial differential equations. in chapter 1, we present a unifying framework for finding profile decompositions in hilbert spaces using the notion of dislocation spaces. the next chapters are then devoted to my publications.   in the second chapter, we construct solutions to the focusing, energy-critical, nonlinear wave equation in dimension 4 and 5, exhibiting finite-time type ii blow-up precisely at the origin with a single profile and a prescribed polynomial blow-up rate of order $-1-ν$, where $ν> 1$ in 4d and $ν> 3$ in 5d. the major difference between dimension 4 and 5 consists in the renormalization procedure. in 4d, we essentially follow the krieger-schlag-tataru scheme developed for the 3-dimensional equation, where the polynomial structure of the nonlinearity permits the use of simple algebraic manipulations to control error terms. by contrast, the 5d case requires a modified setup due to the lower regularity of the nonlinearity, which complicates the treatment of nonlinear error terms.   in chapter 3, we provide a modern presentation of classical lp and schauder estimates for parabolic equations. then, in chapter 4, we consider finite-time and $k$-equivariant solutions to the harmonic map heat flow from a disk to a sphere. under general time-dependent, $k$-equivariant and smooth boundary data, we prove that the profile decomposition at the singular time contains only one bubble. the method relies on the maximum and comparison principle. we also prove a global existence criterion and exhibit solutions blowing up in infinite time for any degree of equivariance. finally, the appendix presents the profile decomposition for the harmonic map heat flow proved by struwe and qing using energy arguments and the palais-smale condition.

title: orbital stability and instability of standing waves for an inhomogeneous logarithmic schrödinger equation
abstract: we study the inhomogeneous logarithmic schrödinger equation \[ i\partial_tu+δu+|x|^{-1}u\log|u|^2=0, \qquad (t,x)\in\r\times\r^n,\quad n\ge2. \] for every initial datum in $h^1(\r^n)$, we establish global existence of weak solutions. we also construct explicit positive stationary solutions and solve the associated nehari minimization problem. for $ω\ge0$, the minimizer is unique up to {a constant} phase and is given by \[ e^{\frac{n-1}{2}(1+\sqrt{1+ω})} e^{-(1+\sqrt{1+ω})|x|}, \] whereas for $ω<0$ the infimum is zero and is not attained. finally, we prove that the standing waves associated with these profiles are orbitally stable for $ω>0$ by a variational argument, and orbitally unstable for $-1<ω<-1+(n-1)^{-2}$ by combining spectral analysis, localized energy and mass estimates, and phase modulation.

title: well-posedness and large deviations for 3d primitive equations with jumps
abstract: we establish the global pathwise well-posedness and a freidlin--wentzell large deviation principle for the three-dimensional viscous primitive equations driven by multiplicative lévy noise represented by a compensated poisson random measure. under local lipschitz and moment growth assumptions on the noise coefficient, we construct local martingale solutions and obtain a unique maximal pathwise solution with càdlàg trajectories in the $h^1$ energy space. additional sixth-moment growth in $h^1$ and $l^6$ growth bounds on the baroclinic component of the noise yield global pathwise well-posedness. the proof combines the jump itô formula with baroclinic and anisotropic energy estimates to rule out finite-time blow-up. under further exponential integrability and structural assumptions on the noise coefficient, we establish a freidlin--wentzell large deviation principle in a strong path topology by the weak convergence approach.

title: infinitely many nonradial positive solutions for two-coupled nonlinear schrödinger equations in $\bbr^n$ without symmetry
abstract: in this paper, we consider the following two-coupled nonlinear schrödinger equations: \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} &-δu+p(x)u=μu^3+βuv^2,\quad\text{in }\r^n,\\ &-δv+q(x)v=νv^3+βu^2v,\quad\text{in }\r^n,\\ &u,\,v\in h^1(\r^n) \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $n=2,3$, $p(x)$ and $q(x)$ are potentials, $μ$ and $ν$ are positive coefficients and $β\in\r\setminus\{0\}$ is the coupling parameter. by developing the intermediate reduction arguments in [del pino-wei-yao, calc. var., 2015], we prove the existence of infinitely many nonradial positive solutions to the above system under suitable regularity and decay conditions on $p(x)$ and $q(x)$, {\bf but without any symmetry assumptions on them}. the scalar version of our result also gives {\bf a positive answer} to the first part of [question~3, del pino-wei-yao, calc. var., 2015] and our method might be helpful in studying other problems.

title: critical curve for three-dimensional radial wave systems with distinct speeds
abstract: we study radially symmetric solutions to the three-dimensional semilinear wave system with distinct propagation speeds \[   u_{tt}-c_1^2δu=|v_t|^p\ , \   v_{tt}-c_2^2δv=|u_t|^q\ ,   \ c_1, c_2>0\ , c_1\neq c_2\ . \] for \(1<p,q<2\), we prove that \[   γ(p,q)   =   2+\max\left\{\frac1p,\frac1q\right\}-pq=0 \] is the exact critical curve separating small-data global existence from finite-time blow-up. more precisely, sufficiently small, compactly supported radial initial data give rise to global solutions when $γ(p,q)<0$. on the other hand, for a class of initial data, the corresponding solutions blow up in finite time, with an upper bound for the lifespan, when $γ(p,q)\geq 0$.

title: global well-posedness for the energy-critical focusing nls on $\mathbb t^3$
abstract: we prove global well-posedness for the focusing quintic nonlinear schrödinger equation on the standard three-dimensional torus for initial data below the mass-corrected energy and sobolev-norm thresholds determined by the euclidean ground state. this gives a subthreshold focusing counterpart to the defocusing theorem of ionescu and pausader. the proof combines the periodic profile analysis with the recent nonradial euclidean scattering theorem of su and zhao. the mass correction yields an invariant region and a nonnegative energy decomposition, placing every euclidean profile below both ground-state thresholds. uniform bounds on finite intervals follow from a contradiction argument on shrinking time intervals.

title: liouville systems i: blow-up analysis and orthogonal decomposition
abstract: we study blow-up solutions of generalized liouville systems on a closed surface at and near critical parameter hypersurfaces. under a morse assumption on the reduced functional, we establish the following results.   first, we introduce amplitude variables in the approximate manifold and prove that every sequence of blow-up solutions at a fixed critical parameter, or along an admissible sequence from the lower side, admits a unique minimizing decomposition up to permutation. the remainder converges to zero and is orthogonal to the center, scale, and amplitude directions. the concentration scales are comparable, the limiting configuration satisfies the scale balance conditions, and the amplitudes vanish after multiplication by the logarithmic scale. second, we determine the leading parameter defect in both critical decay regimes and prove that, along each fixed admissible path, all sufficiently large solutions lie in finitely many disjoint bubbling neighborhoods. finally, assuming the leading coefficient is nonzero at every balanced critical configuration, the solution set at the fixed critical parameter is compact.   these results provide the analytic foundation for studying the resonant degree via critical points at infinity.

title: multiplicity via symmetry for the minkowski mean curvature equation: dirichlet and neumann problems
abstract: we consider the minkowski mean curvature equation $$ -\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right) =λu+μh(x,u) \quad \text{in } ω, \quad \mathcal b u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial ω, $$ where $\mathcal b \in \{ \mathcal d, \mathcal n \}$ is a dirichlet or neumann boundary condition and $ω$ is a smooth bounded domain, required to be convex in the neumann case. moreover, $λ, μ\geq0$ are parameters, and $h(x,u)$ is odd with respect to $u$ and positive for $u > 0$. using minmax methods in nonsmooth critical point theory, we prove that $λ>λ^\mathcal b_k$ yields at least $k$ pairs of nontrivial solutions with negative energy for every $μ\geq0$, where $λ_k^\mathcal b$ are the corresponding laplacian eigenvalues, indexed by $λ^\mathcal b_0=0$. moreover, if $h(x,u):=\int_0^u h(x,t)\,dt=o(u^2)$ as $u\to0$, we prove that for $λ\in[λ^\mathcal b_k,λ^\mathcal b_{k+1})$ and every $j\geq\max\{1,k\}$, sufficiently large $μ$ yields at least $2j-k$ distinct pairs of solutions: $j$ with negative energy and $j-k$ with positive energy.

title: hypocoercivity for a thermostatted boltzmann equation
abstract: we study the boltzmann equation for a gas on the three-dimensional torus. its particles collide with one another and with a thermal reservoir whose temperature varies in space. the reservoir heats the gas in some regions and cools it in others, driving a nonequilibrium energy current. for the isotropic cutoff kernel, with maxwell molecules or hard potentials, we prove global well-posedness and exponential convergence to the same stationary state for initial data with a common gaussian upper bound and gaussian moment bound. these bounds determine how weak self collisions must be relative to bath collisions. the estimates are uniform over bath profiles between fixed positive temperature bounds. for any nonconstant reservoir profile on the three-dimensional torus, this stationary state cannot be a local maxwellian. when particles collide only with the bath, relative entropy to the stationary state cannot increase. once self collisions are added, arbitrarily small perturbations can initially increase it, even though they later return exponentially.

title: non-isothermal plane couette flow for the boltzmann equation in three dimensions
abstract: we study the boltzmann equation for a non-isothermal plane couette flow in the three-dimensional channel $\mathbb t_x\times(-1,1)_y\times\mathbb t_z$ for maxwell molecules. for sufficiently small shear rate and wall temperature perturbations, we construct a unique steady solution near the global maxwellian. for the corresponding unsteady boundary value problem, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of solutions arising from small perturbations of the steady state, together with their exponential convergence to the steady state as $t\to\infty$. a major difficulty in both the steady and unsteady problems is to close the outgoing mass fluxes generated by diffuse reflection. to overcome this difficulty, we develop a new boundary flux transmission framework which, in the slab geometry, yields steady and time-dependent wall flux estimates through the boundary-to-boundary transmission between the two walls. we further extend this framework to damped transport equations with diffuse reflection in general bounded $c^1$ domains, even when the damping coefficient degenerates at large velocities.

title: eccentricity distribution of extreme mass ratio inspirals
abstract: we present realistic eccentricity distributions for extreme mass ratio inspirals (emris) forming via the two-body relaxation channel in nuclear star clusters, tracking their evolution up to the final plunge onto the central schwarzschild massive black hole (mbh). we find that emris can retain significant eccentricities at plunge, with a distribution peaking at $e_\mathrm{pl} \approx0.2$, and a considerable fraction reaching much higher values. in particular, up to $20\%$ of the forming emris feature $e_\mathrm{pl} > 0.5$ for central mbh masses $m_\bullet$ in the range $10^5 \mathrm{m_\odot} \leq m_\bullet \leq 10^6 \mathrm{m_\odot}$, partially due to emris forming at large semi-major axes and "cliffhanger emri", usually neglected in literature. this highlights the importance of accounting for eccentricity in waveform modeling and detection strategies for future space-based gravitational wave observatories such as the upcoming laser interferometer space antenna (lisa). furthermore, we find that the numerical fluxes in energy and angular momentum currently implemented in the fastemriwaveforms (few) package may not adequately sample the full parameter space relevant to low-mass mbhs ($m_\bullet < 10^6 \mathrm{m_\odot}$), potentially limiting its predictive power in that regime. specifically, for $m_\bullet=10^5 \mathrm{m_\odot}$ we find that about $75\%$ ($50 \%$) of emris at 2 years (6 months) from plunge fall outside the currently available flux parameter space. our findings motivate the development of extended flux grids and improved interpolation schemes to enable accurate modeling of emris across a broader range of system parameters.

title: schwarzschild spacetime and the local limit of nonlocal gravity
abstract: we investigate static spherically symmetric solutions within the framework of the local limit of nonlocal gravity. this theory departs from einstein's general relativity (gr) through the introduction of a scalar gravitational susceptibility function $s(x)$, $1+s > 0$, which is a new feature of the spacetime that vanishes in the gr limit. it is shown that the schwarzschild spacetime constitutes an exact solution of the modified source-free gravitational field equations provided $s$ is a constant. the mass of the corresponding schwarzschild solution is given by $m/(1+s)$, where $m$ denotes the mass of the solution in the gr limit. the interpretation of the solution in terms of a black hole is ruled out due to the divergence of the algebraic invariants of the weitzenböck torsion at the schwarzschild horizon.

title: modified gravity at large scales on quantum spacetime in the ikkt model
abstract: the gravitational dynamics of 3+1 dimensional covariant quantum spacetime in the ikkt or iib matrix model is studied at one loop, combining the yang-mills-type matrix action with the induced einstein-hilbert action. this combined action leads to interesting modifications of the gravitational dynamics at long distances, governed by modified einstein equations including an extra geometrical tensor interpreted as ''mirage matter''. in particular we find extra non-ricci flat geometric modes with a non-standard dispersion relation, with features reminiscent of dark matter and/or dark energy.

title: spinning compact object and chaos in galactic centres
abstract: galactic centres are extremely complex environments, consisting primarily of a supermassive black hole (smbh) surrounded by asymmetric mass distributions such as nuclear star clusters (nsc) and molecular gas, which form disks or halos. together these components exert a gravitational field which, combined with relativistic corrections from the spin of the smbh, generates strongly nonlinear dynamics and chaotic orbits. we model this region using a multipolar expansion potential, in which the central compact object is represented by the artemova-björnsson-novikov pseudo-newtonian potential, which mimics the spin dependence of a kerr-like bh. the surrounding halo is modelled as an axisymmetric, shell-like mass distribution expanded to dipole order to induce asymmetry. previous works have mostly quantified the chaos caused by the bh spin and dipole moment using poincaré sections, sali and other chaos indicators. in this study, we incorporate stability analysis and newton-raphson basins of convergence to provide a global view of the dynamics of the system. stability analysis around fixed points gives deeper insight into the local behaviour, while basins of convergence show sensitivity to initial conditions and reveal fractal boundaries. our results show that the bh spin substantially reshapes the equilibrium landscape. depending on its magnitude, it can either intensify the chaos induced by the halo asymmetry or simplify the phase space. these results improve our understanding of how relativistic spin effects and multipole moments collectively affect particle motion in galactic centres.

title: cosmological discrete self-similarity in primordial black hole formation
abstract: we demonstrate that discrete self-similarity (dss), originally discovered in the asymptotically flat collapse of a massless scalar field, survives in primordial black hole (pbh) formation within an expanding cosmological background. using fully relativistic simulations of massless scalar-field collapse in a friedmann-lemaître-robertson-walker universe, we resolve the near-critical regime and find clear log-periodic oscillations in the pbh mass-scaling relation. this result provides a proof of principle that pbhs may retain information about the critical behaviour in their formation realized in the early universe: pbh formation in scalar-field kination exhibits dss, while radiation-fluid collapse is characterized by continuous self-similarity. the resulting mass scaling imprints characteristic log-periodic modulations in an illustrative pbh mass spectrum, which may survive when pbh formation is dominated by a sufficiently narrow range of scales, with possible consequences for pbh phenomenology. our results show that pbhs may encode not only the amplitude of primordial perturbations, but also the nature of the matter sector and the dynamical state of the universe at horizon re-entry.

title: critical collapse remains discretely self-similar at large d
abstract: when matter collapses at the threshold of black hole formation spacetime typically has an emergent continuous or discrete symmetry, depending on the matter content. for the einstein-klein-gordon model in any finite dimension d>3 the associated critical spacetime solutions exhibit discrete self-similarity, characterized by the echoing period delta. combining analytical and numerical results with dimensions up to d=200 we predict delta remains finite at infinite dimension d, contrary to a recent conjecture. we find the fit delta=1.6439+10.37/d-o(1/d^2) and provide an explicit large-d model.

title: analytic marginalization over calibration uncertainties in gravitational wave inference and application to black hole ringdown
abstract: the uncertain calibration of gravitational wave detectors is one source of systematic error in gravitational wave inference. while generally small, this uncertainty can be accounted for by modeling and marginalizing over calibration corrections. in this work we extend the standard frequency-domain approach to calibration marginalization to the time domain using basis splines, in such a way that the marginalization is analytic. we apply this method to the time-domain analysis of black hole ringdown, in particular the two highest signal-to-noise events detected so far, gw250114 and gw250207. for gw250114 we continue to find strong evidence for two ringdown modes, after marginalizing over the small calibration uncertainty at the time of the event. for gw250207, the calibration of the ligo-hanford detector was uncertain, and calibration marginalization is required for a coherent analysis using both ligo detectors. we find that when calibration effects are included the remnant mass and spins inferred during ringdown agree with inferences from the full signal. despite the high signal-to-noise of gw250207, we find no evidence for the presence of a second mode in the ringdown, and as a result deviations from relativity during ringdown are not well constrained.

title: the goldilocks prior: physically consistent inference of neutron star properties from gravitational wave observations
abstract: gravitational wave observations of neutron star mergers provide a unique window into the interiors of neutron stars, probing dense matter from microscopic nuclear interactions to the macroscopic structure, including their maximum mass, beyond which the remnant collapses to a black hole. accurate inference of these properties is crucial, as many astrophysical, nuclear, and multimessenger studies rely on gravitational wave constraints. studies on estimating neutron-star properties from gravitational waves often employ priors that neglect correlations between parameters, or treat tidal degrees of freedom inconsistently, leading to biases in inferred neutron-star properties. we introduce a novel physically informed prior, goldilocks prior, that is informed by a broad, semi-parametric ensemble of equations of state, accounts for the joint correlations among the chirp mass, mass ratio, and both tidal deformability parameters, and is tailored to detector sensitivity. using several mock binary neutron star merger simulations spanning symmetric and asymmetric masses, spinning and non-spinning systems, and a range of signal-to-noise ratios, we show that goldilocks prior consistently reduces biases in the inferred tidal posteriors relative to uniform and previously proposed eos-informed priors. this framework provides a robust, systematic approach for neutron star parameter estimation, enabling more reliable inference for both current and future gravitational wave observations.

title: noncommutative kazakov-solodukhin gravastar
abstract: we construct a thin-shell gravastar with a de sitter interior and a phenomenological exterior combining a lorentzian noncommutative-inspired mass distribution with the unexpanded kazakov--solodukhin deformation. within an effective einstein description, we derive the surface stresses, evaluate the shell energy conditions, and compute transparent-shell geodesics using a single exterior metric. the associated horizon-bearing family satisfies a radial-pressure thermodynamic identity with area entropy. for the gravastar, the first three penetrating visibility boundaries move inward with increasing ks scale, while the exterior photon orbit and critical impact parameter move outward. a finite-observer backlighting calculation reproduces the schwarzschild--de sitter benchmark and tracks the merger of visibility boundaries as the shell moves beyond the photon orbit. we also compute the redshift-weighted intensity of a face-on, optically thin emitting layer. additional disk crossings after core transmission produce inner image structure whose brightness depends on the radial emission profile. at leading inverse-radius order, both deformation scales enter through one coefficient, producing an exact geometric parameter degeneracy. we show that the next inverse-radius term breaks this degeneracy: the critical impact parameter and logarithmic strong-deflection coefficient provide independent local information about the two scales. full-metric calculations for equal-leading-coefficient parameter pairs resolve this splitting and quantify the accuracy of the higher-order expansion.

title: a transformer model for precessing binary black-hole merger waveforms calibrated to numerical relativity
abstract: we present a transformer model for merger-centered gravitational waveforms from precessing binary black holes. given the mass ratio and two three-dimensional spin vectors, the network predicts quintic b-spline coefficients for all 21 signed spin-weighted spherical-harmonic strain modes through $\ell=4$ on $[-1100,80]m$ ($m$ being the total binary mass), enforcing binary-exchange and equatorial-reflection equivariance and yielding $c^4$ waveforms in time with exact automatic differentiation. the model is pretrained on numerical-relativity (nr) waveforms from the sxs and rit catalogues together with synthetic nrsur7dq4, seobnrv5phm, and perturbative waveforms, and fine-tuned on sxs strain data. on 176 held-out sxs waveforms (165 physical systems), it achieves a mean balanced root-mean-square strain error of $0.023$ and a mean detector mismatch at $120\,m_\odot$ of $0.059\%$.

title: tidal love numbers of thin-shell wormholes, de sitter gravastars, and anti-de sitter gravastars via full perturbed junction conditions
abstract: in this work, we revisit the tidal love numbers (tlns) of several classes of exotic compact objects (ecos) using the recently derived full perturbed junction conditions. we investigate four representative thin-shell models: wormholes, de sitter gravastars with zero surface energy density, general de sitter gravastars, and anti-de sitter gravastars. previous studies of wormholes and de sitter gravastars with zero surface energy density, based on simplified matching conditions, suggested that the tlns of ultracompact ecos vanish logarithmically in the black-hole (bh) limit, leading to the conjecture that this logarithmic dependence is a generic feature of ultracompact exotic objects. we show that this logarithmic behavior is not universal once the full perturbed junction conditions are imposed. in particular, the odd-parity tlns exhibit polynomial scaling in the bh limit for all the models considered, while the even-parity sector displays both logarithmic and polynomial behaviors depending on the model. we also find that the signs of the tlns can differ qualitatively from previous results, especially in the odd-parity sector. our results demonstrate that the tidal response of ecos is strongly affected by the perturbed matching conditions and that the previously conjectured universal logarithmic scaling near the bh limit is not generic.

title: algebraic representation of general relativity in harmonic gauge
abstract: we present a self-contained coordinate-matrix formulation of general relativity in the harmonic gauge, providing a compact, index-free representation of the gravitational field equations within the algebra of $4\times 4$ real matrices $m_4$. by defining musical isomorphism operators ($\sharp, \flat$), metric adjoints ($\dagger$), and matrix-valued derivative vectors ($\bm{\mathcal{b}}, \bm{\mathcal{c}}, \bm{\mathcal{d}}^\sharp$), the ricci tensor is recast into an algebraic matrix structure dominated by the laplace--beltrami operator $\box_{\mathrm{lb}} \coloneqq \operatorname{tr}(\mathcal{g}^\sharp \partial^2)$, where $\partial^2 \coloneqq \bm{\partial}\bm{\partial}^t$ represents the matrix hessian operator of second partial derivatives. within this setting, einstein's field equations naturally take the form of a non-linear wave equation for the metric matrix $\mathcal{g}$, giving rise to an index-free matrix representation of the gravitational energy-momentum pseudotensor $\bar{\mathcal{t}}$. we derive the explicit algebraic relation connecting $\bar{\mathcal{t}}$ with the classical landau--lifshitz energy-momentum complex $\mathcal{t}_{\mathrm{ll}}$, and express the associated local conservation law in a simple matrix divergence form, $\bm{\partial}^t \left((-g)(\mathcal{t}^{\sharp} + \mathcal{t}_{\mathrm{ll}}^{\sharp})\right) = \bm{0}^t$. finally, we illustrate the scope and applicability of the matrix formalism through three physical applications: weak-field linearized gravity, the exact derivation of friedmann cosmological dynamics in harmonic time, and the complete formulation of linear scalar cosmological perturbations in both the newtonian and harmonic gauges.

title: circular motion and fundamental frequencies of charged particles in dipole magnetic field around magnetized bocharova--bronnikov--melnikov--bekenstein black holes
abstract: we examine the field produced by a stationary current loop encircling a static bocharova--bronnikov--melnikov--bekenstein (bbmb) black hole and the response of charged test particles. from the dipole projection of maxwell's equations, we obtain closed-form interior and exterior radial functions, and we test them against a multipole expansion of the localized source whose radial functions are also elementary. every horizon-regular mode vanishes at the degenerate horizon $r_+=m$, so the magnetic flux through the horizon is zero. for a loop at $r_0=10m$, the dipole errors in the equatorial potential and polar field remain below $10\%$ for $r\lesssim0.42\,r_0$ and $r\gtrsim3.02\,r_0$, but reach about $40\%$ and $80\%$ close to the loop. using the resulting potential, we study the effective potential, circular orbits, the innermost stable circular orbit (isco), a binding-energy proxy, and epicyclic frequencies. because the dipole field reverses its equatorial direction across the loop, a positive magnetic coupling $\mathcal{b}$ acts oppositely on the two sides. above $\mathcal{b}_c\simeq0.0119$, the prograde radially stable orbits split into two bands separated by an unstable gap. at $\mathcal{b}=0.2$, the isco moves from $4m$ to $2.97m$, the exterior band begins at $45.46m$, and the isco binding-energy proxy grows from $8.14\%$ to $23.39\%$, compared with $5.72\%$ for neutral particles around a schwarzschild black hole. for negative coupling, exterior orbits can be radially stable but vertically unstable. higher multipoles preserve the large-coupling trends but shift the near-loop values appreciably, so the near-loop results apply to the projected source rather than to a thin ring.

title: can absorption enhance differences between black-hole images?
abstract: we investigate whether absorption can enhance morphological differences between images of different spacetimes, particularly when their critical impact parameters are similar. using a phenomenological thick-accretion-flow model with an effective absorption coefficient $χ_0$, we compare schwarzschild black-hole images with those of bardeen, hayward, and ayón-beato--garcía black holes. in the face-on schwarzschild--bardeen comparison with $g/m=0.5$, the dominant brightness shifts from a narrow lensed feature to a broader outer feature at $χ_0m\simeq$0.585 and 0.717, respectively. near the first transition, the integrated difference between independently normalized images increases by $23.5$% on a common physical grid and by $46.6$% after rescaling by the respective critical impact parameters. enhancement occurs across all three regular-black-hole families and over a broad range of the sampled flow parameters and viewing inclinations, although its magnitude and occurrence depend on the prescribed flow. asynchronous brightness-peak transitions alone are insufficient to guarantee enhancement. these results suggest that the opacity dependence of image morphology may provide information complementary to the critical-curve scale, potentially helping distinguish spacetimes with similar characteristic shadow sizes. assessing this possibility observationally requires physically consistent, frequency-dependent radiative transfer.

title: rational orbits and gravitational-wave signatures around a horndeski black hole
abstract: we study equatorial timelike geodesics and associated gravitational-wave (gw) emission for a static horndeski black hole with secondary scalar hair, characterized by an effective pressure parameter $p_{\mathrm{eff}}$. using the rational-orbit taxonomy $(z,w,v)$, we analyze the innermost stable circular orbit (isco), marginally bound orbit (mbo), and periodic bound orbits. we find that increasing $p_{\mathrm{eff}}$ systematically shifts orbital radii outward and modifies the rational parameter $q$. within the test-particle and quadrupole approximations, we estimate gw signals from an extreme mass-ratio inspiral (emri) system at a luminosity distance of $d_l=8000\,\mathrm{pc}$. the characteristic strains reach $\sim10^{-18}$ in the mhz band, partially overlapping the nominal lisa sensitivity range. these results demonstrate that horndeski corrections systematically alter strong-field orbital dynamics and gw spectra, offering a phenomenological probe of deviations from general relativity.

title: gravitational thermodynamicization of primordial black holes: an rvb residue formulation of thermal formation and nonequilibrium evolution
abstract: we establish a controlled, local, and quasi-stationary thermodynamic framework for neutral, nonrotating primordial black holes (pbhs) by combining a local residue prescription with the thermodynamicization of gravitational dynamics. for a nonextremal spherical horizon, we demonstrate that the positive residue of a meromorphic one-form directly determines the inverse hawking temperature. applying the first law of thermodynamics recovers the standard schwarzschild temperature and bekenstein-hawking entropy under standard normalization. the resulting entropy defines an off-shell canonical exponent, which reveals that equilibrium thermal production of pbhs is exponentially suppressed in a radiation-dominated universe, thereby confirming that the standard density-perturbation collapse criterion remains the primary formation mechanism. for post-formation evolution, we adopt a detailed-balance mass law, prove the validity of the generalized second law of thermodynamics, and express the evolution dynamics as a free-energy gradient flow where the moving mass acts as an instantaneous evaporation-accretion threshold. finally, we derive explicit first-order shifts for the temperature, entropy, thermal saddle, and nucleation exponent under small analytic deformations of the residue.

title: an orbital curvature for iscos
abstract: building on the fact that circular orbits are the fixed points of the phase portraits arising from the geodesic equations on a black hole spacetime, we develop a general orbital geometry, which captures the stability structure of orbits. the construction uses the orbital energy, angular momentum and angular velocity as state space variables, with response functions encoding how the circular orbits react to changes in the black hole background and in their angular motion. the associated scalar curvature provides a geometric diagnostic of certain distinguished points of the circular orbit family, including, the innermost stable circular orbit (isco), where it becomes singular. across the isco, the relevant orbital response functions change sign as the system passes from the stable to the unstable circular orbit branch, and typically vanish at marginal stability. we illustrate the framework for schwarzschild black holes in asymptotically flat four dimensions, and five dimensional schwarzschild ads spacetimes. in the four-dimensional case, the isco is associated with a degeneration of the energy response sector, while in the five dimensional ads case it is detected through the angular response. the ads example also exhibits a separate curvature singularity at a point which coincides with the minimum temperature of the black hole background. these results show that the orbital response geometry provides a unified geometric framework for characterizing the stability of circular orbits and criticality of iscos.

title: a smoothly truncated dark matter spike around a black hole in an einstein-cluster model
abstract: we introduce a finite dark matter spike around a static, spherically symmetric black hole, with a general power-law index and an einstein-cluster stress tensor. smooth inner depletion and outer truncation ensure that the density and its first radial derivative vanish at both boundaries, while a single normalization preserves the prescribed exterior mass. the resulting spacetime contains an inner vacuum gap, a matter region with vanishing radial pressure, and an outer schwarzschild vacuum. we derive the enclosed mass, density maximum, local logarithmic slope, and matched metric without surface layers, including exact polynomial-root representations of the matter-region metric for spike indices $7/3$ and $3/2$. energy conditions and radial stability of the constituent circular orbits constrain the admissible configurations. a sufficient bound guarantees these properties for an inner edge at or beyond the schwarzschild marginal-stability radius and also ensures positivity of the massless-scalar potential. comparisons at a common mass budget examine how boundary regularity and radial concentration jointly affect the gravitational response. shadows and light deflection also depend on the global redshift and mass calibration. scalar waves matched across the three regions with one infinity-normalized time coordinate distinguish local gap-redshift effects from propagation through the complete geometry. the smoothly truncated profile provides a controlled equilibrium model for investigating how finite support and mass redistribution affect black hole observables; its taper scales, formation, and collective stability require additional physical input.

title: instabilities of simpson-visser black bounces sourced by a phantom scalar and nonlinear electrodynamics
abstract: we study the linear stability of simpson-visser ``black-bounce'' space-times (regular black holes and wormholes) under spherically symmetric (monopole) perturbations, taking as a source a phantom scalar field with a self-interaction potential and a magnetic field within nonlinear electrodynamics (ned). the metric contains two parameters: the mass $m$ and the bounce parameter $a >0$, such that $a \leq 2m$ corresponds to black holes and $a > 2m$ to wormholes. the stability problem reduces to a boundary-value problem for a schrödinger-like equation with a certain effective potential. all space-times under study are found to be unstable, and the corresponding exponential growth rates are calculated. for black holes the results are obtained without complications, while the wormhole stability problem faces difficulties that seem to be previously unnoticed. thus, the darboux transformation, used to remove the wall shaped $\approx 2/z^2$ in the effective potentials at wormhole throats ($z$ is the tortoise coordinate), creates nonphysical poles outside the throat for $a/(2m) \lesssim 4.98$. we circumvent this difficulty by using a gauge-invariant approach in the spirit of cremona, pizzocchero and sarbach, leading to a master equation with a simple and regular potential. its further analysis reveals unstable modes: the mode with a variable throat radius is always present; for $a/(2m) \gtrsim 4.98$ there are two real growing throat modes, which merge into a complex-conjugate pair (oscillatory instability) for smaller $a$. a further analysis reveals three exceptional points that separate ranges of $a/(2m)$ with different perturbation regimes. furthermore, the leading unstable black-hole and wormhole modes approach the same limiting growth rate $mκ\simeq 0.10121$ as $a/(2m)$ approaches unity from either side.

title: the three-dimensional galilean black hole
abstract: we report a novel solution of three-dimensional galilean anti-de sitter gravity. the theory can be formulated as a topological gauge theory invariant under the doubly extended newton-hooke group in three dimensions. the solution possesses four conserved charges: energy, angular momentum, spin and rest mass. interestingly, the magnitude of the spin turns out to bounded from above by the rest mass. the solution exhibits the thermal properties that define a black hole configuration in terms of its gauge theoretical description. temperature, angular velocity and other chemical potentials are obtained from suitable regularity conditions associated with the topology of the euclidean continuation of the solution. at zero temperature, an extreme configuration is shown to emerge provided the bound between the spin and the rest mass saturates.

title: bondi-sachs formalism on past light cones and an analogue of the integral mass formula
abstract: following a proposal that the thermodynamic aspects of general relativity can be found in the evolution of the past light cones of arbitrary worldlines, we generalize the bondi-sachs formalism to these surfaces. the observer may accelerate and rotate their tetrad, the spacetime may contain matter and a cosmological constant, and no symmetry is assumed. we impose regularity conditions at the vertex of each light cone and along the polar axis, including a general axial condition that allows for shear. given a suitable prescription for the stresses of matter, the einstein field equations can then be integrated hierarchically from data on a single light cone, and the regularity at the vertex fixes all constants of integration. the solution reveals a universal property: to first order in the observer's proper time, the evolution of the metric and of the four-momentum crossing the light cones is independent of the specific behavior of matter. as an application, we derive, for an observer immersed in matter, an analogue of the integral mass formula of black hole mechanics.

title: natural potentials for tt tensors, divergence-free symmetric tensors and linearised relativistic initial data
abstract: let $n$ be a natural tensor which vanishes at a metric $g\_0$. by diffeomorphism invariance, $dn(g\_0)^*$ takes values in divergence-free symmetric $2$-tensors, and in tt tensors if moreover $dn(g\_0)$ kills conformal directions. such operators are local potentials, which we call machines: they produce smooth compactly supported tensors with the required property and, on closed manifolds, all of them up to a finite-dimensional space when their symbol is injective. on einstein manifolds of every dimension, the linearised bach tensor gives the operator $p$ of an earlier paper, which factorises on tt tensors into the massless and partially massless spin-$2$ operators; we also construct machines on bach-flat, conformally flat and ricci-parallel metrics. replacing the diffeomorphisms of $m$ by those of the vacuum development, we obtain potentials, with a fredholm property, for the linearised einstein constraint equations on arbitrary spacelike hypersurfaces of minkowski, de sitter and anti-de sitter spacetimes.

title: exponential decays of steklov eigenfunctions for the magnetic laplacian
abstract: consider the dirichlet-to-neumann map $λ_β$ associated with the schrödinger operator $(d+β\a)^2$ with a magnetic potential in a bounded lipschitz domain $ω$, where $β>1$ is the field strength parameter. assume that the magnetic field $\b=\nabla \times \a$ is of finite type. we show that if $β>β_0$, the ground state for $λ_β$ decays exponentially away from a neighborhood of the subset of $\partialω$, on which $\b$ vanishes to the maximal order.

title: on the optimal mass threshold for the two-dimensional keller-segel system coupled to the navier-stokes equations
abstract: we investigate the mass threshold for the two-dimensional keller-segel system coupled with the incompressible navier-stokes equations. in the absence of fluid interaction, the classical keller-segel system admits a well-known $4π$-critical-mass dichotomy: for every suitably regular initial datum of total mass \(m<4π\), the associated no-flux initial-boundary value problem admits a global bounded classical solution, whereas for \(m>4π\), there exist smooth initial configurations of mass $m$ such that the associated solution blows up in finite or infinite time. for the fluid-coupled system, winkler first established global generalized solvability under the condition \(m<2π\) and proposed an open question whether the fluid action may lower the critical blow-up mass to some value lying between $2π$ and $4π$.   in the present work, we resolve this open problem and show that the presence of the fluid does not alter the critical mass threshold, and the entire classical subcritical regime remains intact: every admissible initial datum with total mass \(m<4π\) generates a unique global classical solution that is uniformly bounded with respect to time.   our proof relies on the construction of a new quasi-energy inequality. the key underlying observation is that combining relative isoperimetric estimates with rearrangement techniques yields a gagliardo-nirenberg inequality on bounded planar domains with an explicit leading constant.

title: dynamics of subcritical threshold solutions for the three-dimensional energy-critical nls
abstract: we extend the radial threshold classification of duyckaerts and merle on the lower kinetic branch to nonradial solutions of the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical nonlinear schrödinger equation in \(\dot h^1(\mathbb r^3)\). at the ground state energy and with initial gradient norm strictly below that of the ground state, every solution is global and either scatters in both time directions or is a symmetry transform of the special solution \(w^-\), possibly after conjugate time reversal. the proof combines su and zhao's below-threshold scattering theorem with a coercivity estimate for the interaction form at threshold under a kinetic gap and a local analysis near the ground state orbit.

title: single-scale regularity from dirichlet energy for the five-dimensional stationary navier--stokes equations
abstract: we establish an interior $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion for suitable weak solutions of the unforced stationary navier--stokes equations in an open set $ω\subset\mathbb r^5$. there exists a universal constant $\varepsilon_\ast>0$ such that $x_0$ is regular if, for some ball $b_r(x_0)\subsetω$ with $r>0$, \[ \frac1r\int_{b_r(x_0)}|\nabla u|^2\,dx \leq \varepsilon_\ast^2. \] the main difficulty is that the dirichlet energy controls the velocity oscillation while its mean may be arbitrarily large. subtracting the mean introduces a large constant drift into the perturbation equation. moreover, smallness in $h^1$ alone is insufficient to close a direct nonlinear elliptic estimate in five dimensions. we overcome these difficulties through uniform oseen estimates and a relative-energy comparison yielding quadratic improvement of the perturbation. as a consequence, the singular set has zero one-dimensional upper minkowski content on every compact subset of $ω$, and hence local upper minkowski dimension at most one.

title: trace and regularized index of callias operators on hyperbolic space
abstract: let $d \geq 3$ be odd. on hyperbolic space $\mathbb{h}^d$, we consider callias-type operators, i.e. dirac-schrödinger operators of the form $d = ic \nabla + a$, where $c \nabla$ is the dirac operator and $a$ a function with values in the self-adjoint operators, and provide an explicit formula for the iterated trace $\text{tr}_{l^2(\mathbb{h}^d,h)} \text{tr}_{s}( e^{-td^*d} - e^{-tdd^*})$, $t>0$, that appears in the formulation of the witten index. thereby, the operator $d$ is not assumed to be fredholm.

title: unconditional uniqueness of kdv and mkdv green solutions at low regularity
abstract: we prove unconditional uniqueness for the korteweg--de vries (kdv) equation in $c_th^{-1}_x(\mathbb r)$ and the real defocusing modified kdv equation in $c_tl^2_x(\mathbb r)$ within the class of green solutions, an intrinsically well defined solution notion that encodes the evolution at these low regularities through the diagonal green functions of the associated lax operators. a key contribution is automatic local smoothing: the green identities imply $q\in l^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for kdv and $u_x,u^2\in l^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for mkdv in spacetime, with estimates uniform over spatial translates. the uniqueness results therefore identify every green solution in these classes with the continuous extension of the corresponding schwartz flow.

title: tidal deformability of neutron stars in scalar-tensor theories of gravity
abstract: gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences are valuable for testing theories of gravity in the strong field regime. by measuring neutron star tidal deformability using gravitational waves from binary neutron stars, stringent constraints were placed on the equation of state of matter at extreme densities. tidal love numbers in alternative theories of gravity may differ significantly from their general relativistic counterparts. understanding exactly how the tidal love numbers change will enable scientists to untangle physics beyond general relativity from the uncertainty in the equation of state measurement. in this work, we explicitly calculate the fully relativistic $l \geq 2$ tidal love numbers for neutron stars in scalar-tensor theories of gravitation. we use several realistic equations of state to explore how the mass, radius, and tidal deformability relations differ from those of general relativity. we find that tidal love numbers and tidal deformabilities can differ significantly from those in general relativity in certain regimes. the electric tidal deformability can differ by $\sim 200\%$, and the magnetic tidal deformability differs by $\sim 300 \%$. these deviations occur at large compactnesses ($c = m/r \gtrsim 0.2$) and vary slightly depending on the equation of state. this difference suggests that using the tidal love numbers from general relativity could lead to significant errors in tests of general relativity using the gravitational waves from binary neutron star and neutron-star--black-hole mergers.

title: novel thermodynamic inequality for rotating ads black holes
abstract: we propose a new thermodynamic inequality for stationary, asymptotically anti-de sitter rotating black holes, expressed in terms of their angular momentum, mass and thermodynamic volume as $ 4πj^2/(3mv)<1 $. for the solutions considered, this inequality follows from the requirement that the thermodynamic identities admit a physical horizon with positive area. we examine kerr(-newman)-ads, kerr-sen-ads, pairwise-equal four-charge ads black holes, charged rotating ads black strings, and charged rotating ads c-metrics, finding strong supporting evidence for the inequality across different horizon topologies. we then reformulate the inequality in terms of the underlying metric parameters and compare the resulting constraints with the corresponding regularity and horizon-existence conditions. this analysis shows that the proposed inequality has different physical content for different geometries. we further examine charged super-entropic black holes, for which the ultraspinning limit leads instead to a lower bound on the thermodynamic ratio. this result is consistent with the violation of the reverse isoperimetric inequality characteristic of super-entropic solutions. moreover, when combined with the refined reverse isoperimetric inequality, the proposed bound ensures the physicality of the kerr-ads reference solution entering the refined bound and thereby yields the conventional reverse isoperimetric inequality. we also extend the proposed relation to higher dimensions and test it for singly spinning thin ads black ring with nonspherical horizon topology, finding that the corresponding inequalities are satisfied throughout the thin-ring regime.

title: varying newton constant, entropy and the black hole evaporation law
abstract: we assume that the newton potential of a spherically symmetric body of mass $m$ is $v=-g(m)mr^{-1}$, where the newton constant $g$ may depend on   $m$. we insert this assumption in the schwarzschild solution.   we discuss varying $g$ in the black hole thermodynamics and black hole evaporation law. we extend the bekenstein-hawking formula $\hbar gs=\frac{1}{4}a$, where $s$ is the entropy and $ a$ the area, to a varying $g$. it is shown that if $g(m)$ is of the form of a power-law $g\simeq m^{-γ}$ then $g(m)s\simeq a$ is still preserved but   the evaporation law substantially depends on the function $g(m)$.

title: challenging the weak cosmic censorship with phantom fields
abstract: penrose's weak cosmic censorship conjecture asserts that spacetime singularities produced by gravitational collapse are generically hidden behind event horizons, thus preventing them from causally influencing distant observers and preserving the predictability of the exterior region. in this work, we probe this conjecture in a setup that deliberately violates one of its central assumptions - the dominant energy condition - by considering the spherical collapse of a phantom scalar field with negative energy density. in principle, such a field could produce a schwarzschild geometry with negative mass and therefore no event horizon. our aim is to assess whether, once the dominant energy condition is abandoned, the fully coupled evolution of matter and geometry can dynamically generate or expose naked singularities, thereby probing the robustness of cosmic censorship. to this end, we perform high-accuracy numerical relativity simulations based on fourth-order finite-difference schemes. starting from smooth, asymptotically flat initial data representing regular phantom scalar wave packets, we follow their fully nonlinear evolution through collapse or dispersion. while an ordinary (positive-energy) scalar field exhibits the standard choptuik critical behavior at the threshold of black-hole formation, the phantom field displays qualitatively different dynamics. for all amplitudes considered, we find no evidence for trapped surfaces, naked singularities, or alternative stationary end states. instead, the phantom scalar field disperses in all the configurations studied. within the parameter space explored, we find no dynamical violation of cosmic censorship.

title: kinetic magnetohydrodynamics and landau fluid closure in relativity
abstract: diffuse accretion flows near a supermassive black hole are fundamentally weakly collisional. in such weakly collisional plasmas, the ion and electron distribution functions can deviate significantly from thermal equilibrium, and particle kinetic effects can influence large-scale fluid motion by driving pressure anisotropy, heat conduction, and plasma instabilities. modeling these plasma effects in highly relativistic flows could be important for interpreting horizon-scale observations of black hole images. in this paper, we present a theoretical framework for understanding weakly collisional plasmas in general relativity by deriving the relativistic drift kinetic equations from the vlasov-maxwell equations. we present the evolution equations for the moments of the gyroaveraged distribution function and introduce a new analytic landau fluid closure to capture anisotropic heat flow in relativistic plasmas. unlike standard (collisional) general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics or extended magnetohydrodynamics, our model does not rely on strong collisions to enforce thermal equilibrium and consistently incorporates landau damping in a fluid closure. the model introduced in this work provides a complementary approach to fully kinetic simulations in understanding weakly collisional effects in low-luminosity relativistic black hole accretion disks.

title: oppenheimer-snyder collapse in metric f(r) gravity: constraints from generalized vaidya exteriors
abstract: we study the oppenheimer--snyder (os) collapse problem in metric $f(r)$ gravity by matching a homogeneous dust friedmann--lemaître--robertson--walker (flrw) interior to a generalized vaidya exterior across a timelike hypersurface. in metric $f(r)$ gravity, regular matching requires the continuity not only of the induced metric and extrinsic curvature, but also of the ricci scalar and its normal derivative. {for the homogeneous dust interiors considered here, these additional conditions generically exclude ricci-flat exteriors, such as the schwarzschild solution.} we show that, for an unrestricted generalized vaidya exterior, the matching conditions fix the boundary data but do not uniquely determine the bulk extension, leaving open the possibility of a physical resolution of the collapse problem. however, once the exterior matter content is restricted to the generalized vaidya form, the field equations impose a strong constraint, forcing $f_{,r}$ to be linear in the areal radius, $f_{,r}=a(v)\,r+b(v)$. for locally invertible $f_{,r}$ with $f_{,rr}\neq 0$, this sharply reduces the admissible class of exteriors, so that the matching data uniquely determine the exterior solution on each interval where the boundary map is locally invertible. for branches with $f_{,r}>0$, $f_{,rr}\ne0$, and $f_{,r}$ regular and finite at finite curvature, a globally extended exterior with finite asymptotic curvature requires $a(v)=0$. the matching conditions then force constant curvature. imposing the null energy condition on both sides leaves only the vacuum-energy component and a locally maximally symmetric geometry. under these assumptions, nontrivial collapse of spatially flat flrw perfect-fluid interiors is therefore excluded within the restricted exterior class.

title: stationary solutions in the small-$c$ expansion of gr
abstract: we study the small-$c$ expansion of general relativity in adm variables up to next-to-next-to-leading order (nnlo). we show that, in the stationary sector, this formulation renders the field equations more tractable for explicit solution building. the stationary equations acquire a structure, in which the leading lapse and spatial metric are determined by a closed subsystem, the nlo rotational field satisfies a linear equation on that background, and the nnlo fields satisfy a linear system sourced by the nlo data. the stationary sector exhibits both strong-gravity and weak-field branches, whose structure becomes richer at nnlo. in the strong-gravity branch, we first obtain exact vacuum solutions of nlo carroll gravity, including the lense--thirring and rotating c-metric backgrounds. at nnlo, we then construct the corresponding lense--thirring-type and c-metric-type exact vacuum geometries. these solutions also arise from the small-$c$ expansion of the kerr and rotating c-metric geometries around the strong-gravity background, up to $\mathcal{o}(j)$ at nlo and up to $\mathcal{o}(j^3)$ at nnlo. in the weak-field branch, we find exact hartle--thorne-type solutions with an independent quadrupole moment, together with exact spin-squared corrections and a mixed quadrupolar-rotating solution. we further extend the $\ell=0,2$ sector by including higher multipoles up to $\ell=4$, where $\ell$ denotes the multipole index. these results show that the full nlo/nnlo theory admits a richer stationary vacuum sector than the magnetic carroll truncation. more broadly, the adm formulation provides a practical framework for constructing and analyzing stationary backgrounds in the small-$c$ expansion of general relativity, and may also offer a useful framework for organizing rotational and higher-multipole deformations motivated by relativistic compact-object geometries.

title: relativistic mode sums for neutron-star tidal response
abstract: time-dependent tidal interactions during the late inspiral of binary neutron stars encode valuable information about neutron-star structure, but systematically extending the familiar newtonian mode-sum picture into full general relativity is nontrivial. in this paper, we develop a practical relativistic implementation of mode-sum tidal response for non-rotating neutron stars in regge-wheeler gauge. using near-zone boundary conditions, we systematically define the interior tidal field, the relativistic overlap integrals, and the corresponding mode amplitudes. the good is that the dominant f-mode contribution is remarkably robust, reproducing the direct matching calculation to within $\sim 3$\% across the equations of state we consider. the bad is that the operator governing mode inner product is not positive definite on the full regge-wheeler-gauge function space, so the relativistic mode sum truncated at ${\cal{o}}(ω^2)$ is not expected to strictly converge to the direct matching solution. the subtle is that the tidal field inside the star is not unique, although this ambiguity has only a limited impact on the dominant f-mode response for the classes of extensions studied here. our results establish the practical utility of relativistic mode-sum approximations, while making clear that their predictive power comes from a controlled low-mode description, rather than from a formally convergent strong-field expansion.

title: graviton floor
abstract: it has been observed that the universe is permeated by the cosmic photon background, ranging from radio waves to gamma rays. we investigate the conversion of the photon background into gravitons in the presence of background magnetic fields in the milky way galaxy and in blazar jets. we find that the resulting graviton background is dominated by the contribution generated in blazar jets. importantly, this graviton background constitutes a graviton floor for high-frequency gravitational wave detectors searching for new physics, analogous to the neutrino floor.

title: effects of solar wind plasma noise on stochastic gravitational wave background searches with a space based interferometer network
abstract: the lisa-taiji dual detector network improves millihertz sgwb sensitivity through cross correlation measurements. solar wind plasma, however, can generate plasma noise correlated between detectors and bias sgwb cross correlation estimates. we use high time resolution electron density data from wind/swe, estimate the solar wind electron density fluctuation spectrum with the lomb-scargle method, and propagate the resulting plasma noise to the tdi a/e channels of the lisa-taiji network. by including finite arm propagation, taylor frozen flow spatial correlations, and the network overlap reduction response, we compute the sgwb parameter bias induced by interdetector plasma noise. although the single detector plasma residual is below the reference noise, the component correlated between detectors can enter the sgwb cross correlation estimator directly. under dual detector scale coverage, the plasma induced parameter bias for a power law sgwb can reach $12.73\%$ of the corresponding fisher parameter uncertainty. for m2/m3 cosmic string spectra, the bias in $\ln gμ$ can reach $19.26\%$ of the corresponding fisher parameter uncertainty for the network configurations, observing times, and frequency bands considered here. these results show that the impact of solar wind plasma noise cannot be assessed from the single detector residual noise level alone. in lisa-taiji sgwb searches, the interdetector correlated component of this noise can directly affect parameter estimation.

title: probing rotating einstein-power-yang-mills black holes through shadows and quasinormal modes: prospects for event horizon telescope constraints
abstract: within einstein power-yang-mills gravity (epym), we build a rotating black hole via the newman-janis procedure applied to the spherically symmetric static seed, obtaining an epym-inspired kerr-like metric controlled by the spin \(a\), the magnetic yang-mills charge \(q\), and the power parameter \(q\). we analyse the horizon structure and the photon region, and we compute the shadow as it appears to a remote observer for different values of these parameters. using the published event horizon telescope measurements of m87\(^*\) and sgr a\(^*\), we constrain the yang-mills charge and the power parameter from the angular size and the schwarzschild deviation \(δ\) of the observed images. at the maxwell point \(q = 1\) the spin marginalized likelihood of m87\(^*\) bounds the charge to \(q \lesssim 0.29\,m\) at \(1σ\), while the fixed-spin band intersection at \(a = 0.7\,m\) gives the weaker \(q \lesssim 0.52\,m\) from the m87\(^*\) angular size alone. the bound weakens as \(q \to 3/2\), where the shadow diameter becomes nearly insensitive to the charge. the shadow radius also fixes the limiting absorption cross section at high frequencies and hence the energy emission rate, which is suppressed by the charge and enhanced by the power parameter. we then compute the quasinormal modes of a massless scalar on the rotating background from the leading-order wentzel-kramers-brillouin (wkb) conditions on the teukolsky type radial potential, finding that the oscillation frequency rises and the damping rate falls as the charge or spin increases. the power parameter leaves an imprint on the shadow size and its charge sensitivity and in the quasinormal spectrum the shift is in principle present but lies below the resolution of current detectors.

title: on the nature of oscillating modes of proto-neutron stars
abstract: newborn proto-neutron stars (pns) are potential targets of gravitational wave asteroseismology, the study of the (inner) structure of stars via their oscillation modes. to prepare for the eventual detection of such modes by current and future gravitational wave observatories, theoretical studies have obtained the possible spectrum of oscillations. however, there has been disagreement when it comes to identifying and classifying specific modes according to the physical mechanism that excites them. in this paper, we present a novel scheme to classify the oscillation modes of a newly born pns surrounded by a stalled accretion shock in core-collapse supernovae (ccsne). our classification is physically motivated, as it is based on the energy of the restoring forces of the mode. we investigate the nature of the modes by considering the different regions of the ccsn that they stem from. we apply this scheme to a set of 28 non-rotating 1d, 2d and 3d ccsn simulations performed with two different numerical codes and using different progenitors and equations of state. in that way, we find that there are different families of f-, p- and g-modes in the system, living in different areas. more specifically, we identify two families of f- and p-modes associated with the pns and the shock, respectively, and two families of g-modes originating from the two convectively stable regions, one in the pns core and one near its surface. we also find that the dominant high-frequency emission mode is the f-mode of the pns, associated with the strong density gradient at its surface. our classification procedure is automatic, performs consistently for all the models considered, and paves the way to systematic studies of the dependence of the mode frequencies on the pns properties, with direct application to parameter estimation from future observations of gravitational wave signals.

title: kerr quasinormal modes without variable separation: a two-dimensional hyperboloidal teukolsky solver with physics-informed neural networks
abstract: we use physics-informed neural networks (pinns) to solve the gravitational quasinormal-mode (qnm) eigenvalue problem for kerr spacetime directly in the two-dimensional hyperboloidal formulation of the teukolsky equation. this formulation does not require separation of variables and thus retains the coupled radial--angular structure. such a scheme provides a prototype for calculating the qnms of beyond-kerr black holes for which the perturbation equations are non-separable. sequences with increasing angular momentum are constructed, reaching close to the extremal limit. we focus on the fundamental modes $(\ell,m,n)=(2,0,0)$, $(2,1,0)$, $(2,2,0)$, $(3,3,0)$ and $(4,4,0)$, together with the first two overtones $(2,2,1)$ and $(2,2,2)$. after training, the frequency at every spin is refined by solving the discretized equation for it, so that it depends much less on where the stochastic training happens to stop. comparison with continued-fraction values shows that every reported real and imaginary frequency component of the production network remains below $0.23\%$ error, with a median deviation of $2\times10^{-4}\%$. for the fundamental modes, both components agree within about $10^{-3}\%$ up to $a/m=0.97$, and the real parts within $5\times10^{-4}\%$ at every spin. sub-percent accuracy is maintained in the near-extremal regime, where the damping rate becomes small and the modes are longest-lived; there the damping errors grow, and the largest, $0.23\%$, belongs to the $(2,2,1)$ overtone. the results establish a non-spectral numerical route to multidimensional black-hole perturbation eigenproblems which does not match the substantially higher precision of dedicated kerr solvers but offers greater flexibility and requires less analytical pre-processing. the proposed approach is designed to be applicable to other backgrounds whose perturbation equations do not separate.

title: a note on a high-energy limit of gravitational perturbation theory
abstract: the post-minkowskian expansion of general relativity expands the metric in newton's constant g around flat space-time, but much effort currently focuses on ways to extend its range of applicability by summing the perturbative series to all orders. a regime of particular interest is a specific high-energy limit where a formula derived recently provides the momentum kick of binary scattering problem to all orders, and even suggests an approach towards strong coupling. we show that this is an asymptotic expansion. although the series diverges we give evidence that it is borel summable, and the full function in integral form is finite. as a by-product we determine the transcendentality properties of the coefficients in the expanded expression.

title: exact dynamics of spinning particles and the spin wall in schwarzschild spacetime
abstract: the motion of a spinning test body is governed by the mathisson--papapetrou--dixon equations and deviates from geodesics already at first order in the spin. most studies of this problem truncate the dynamics at linear order; here we solve the equatorial, spin-aligned problem in schwarzschild spacetime at all orders in the spin under the tulczyjew--dixon condition. eliminating the four-velocity casts the system into a closed algebraic form and reduces the motion to a single first-order radial equation. keeping track of both kinematical masses, the norm of the four-momentum and its projection on the velocity, we find that the representative worldline ceases to be timelike on a surface in the space of radius, spin and angular momentum. we call this surface the spin wall. it bounds the radii accessible to a spinning body and is present for every nonvanishing value of the momentum's angular component; only for the purely radial family does it collapse, and that family moves on a geodesic. its position follows in closed form and may lie inside the horizon, enclose it, or reach the exterior, the last possibility arising already at small spin. we also examine how far the pole--dipole truncation remains under control where the wall is accessible. within that regime we determine the circular orbits and their stability, the spin dependence of the marginally stable orbit, and the perihelion advance beyond first order in the spin.

title: gravitational waves from strong first-order phase transitions in an expanding universe
abstract: we investigate the gravitational waves generated by first-order phase transitions (pts) in an expanding universe. using a scalar field-fluid coupled model, we perform three-dimensional lattice numerical simulations of slow first-order pts with strong strength. we observe that the contribution from sound waves to the gravitational wave (gw) signal significantly dominates over that from bubble collisions. the sound wave spectra exhibit two peaks located at the mean bubble separation and the sound-shell width. rotational modes are generated in the fluid during the bubble collisions, and their magnitude grows with the pt strength ($α$). the effective lifetime of the sound-wave source increases for slower pts, decreasing for faster pt with larger $β/h$ and rising with smaller $α$. while the simulated amplitude of normalized gravitational waves is of order $\mathcal{o}(10^{-2})$, in alignment with minkowski-spacetime results, the resulting gw spectra differ markedly from those scenarios.

title: a pipeline for identifying astrophysical signals and instrumental glitches in lisa data
abstract: the laser interferometer space antenna (lisa) is a space-based gravitational wave detector scheduled for launch in the 2030s by the european space agency. operating in the 0.1 mhz to 0.1 hz band, lisa will observe a variety of astrophysical sources including but not limited to supermassive black hole mergers, extreme mass ratio inspirals, and white dwarf binaries. lisa will yield new insights, including supermassive black hole formation, new tests of general relativity, population studies of white dwarfs and others. like all interferometric gravitational wave detectors, lisa data is expected to contain non-astrophysical transients, commonly referred to as glitches. we introduce a two step pipeline that consists of a search algorithm for detecting potential transients in simulated lisa data followed by a machine learning model that classifies the detected transients as gravitational waves or instrumental glitches. this is important for mbhbs with very high masses (around $10^6\ m_{\odot}$) which are transients that could be morphologically similar to lisa glitches in the data. initial results demonstrate a promising ability to classify detected events with an accuracy close to $98\%$. the pipeline also shows the ability to analyze a month of data in under 2 minutes on a laptop. this shows an eventual utility of our pipeline for enabling accurate rapid alerts from low latency searches. it could also support model selection in global-fit analyses by providing an initial summary of the location and type of individual signals. this paper also discusses challenges encountered during training, including limitations of the current framework.

title: equatorial periodic orbits and gravitational wave signatures in weyl geometric gravity black holes
abstract: weyl geometric gravity theory is a gravitational theory with lagrangian density constructed from the square of the weyl curvature scalar and the strength of the weyl vector. the theory can be reformulated as a scalar - vector - tensor theory in the riemann geometry by introducing an auxiliary scalar field, in the presence of a non - minimal coupling between the ricci scalar and the scalar field. assuming that the weyl vector has only a radial component, an exact spherically symmetric black hole type solution of the field equations in the vacuum can be obtained. the solution depends on three arbitrary integration constants. as compared to the case of the schwarzschild black hole, the weyl geometric gravity black hole solution contains two new terms, linear and quadratic, in the radial coordinate. it is the main goal of the present work to investigate astrophysical properties of the weyl geometric black holes by considering the behavior of the timelike geodesics, which allows to explore how the geometric nonmetricity influences the strong-field dynamics of massive test particles as well as the topological structure of the periodic orbits. the resulting gravitational wave emission in extreme mass-ratio inspiral (emri) systems is also considered. our results show that the presence of nonmetricity in weyl geometric gravity leaves distinct and measurable signatures on both the orbital topology and the emitted gravitational waveforms of compact emri systems. these unique temporal and amplitude modulations provide a promising observational avenue for testing the presence of nonmetricity on cosmic scales.

title: weak-field analytical solutions for f(r,l_matt) gravity in a static and spherically symmetric space-time for perfect fluids
abstract: we study the weak-field regime of $f(r,\lmatt)$ gravity for a static and spherically symmetric configuration described by a perfect fluid, whose energy density is perturbed about a constant reference value. by means of a weak-field limit expansion about a minkowski geometric background and under a quasi-newtonian approximation, we derive and analytically solve the coupled system that governs the gravitational perturbations and the matter variables.   the solution contains the long-range newtonian contribution and yukawa-type corrections in the temporal and radial components of the metric. in the matter sector, the energy density, the internal energy, and the pressure acquire radial contributions, with a non-zero constant background rest-mass energy density and vanishing background internal energy and pressure. the results show how the non-minimal coupling between curvature and matter jointly modifies the geometry and the fluid in the considered regime.

title: the weyl tensor for gravitational-wave causal sets: thickness of geodesic analogs and geodesic deviation
